newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm, expected steady on the day.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm, expected steady on the day.

text.p: Speculative local buying nudged leading Russian shares slightly higher in the early hours of trade on Friday, dealers said, but they saw little change in prices over the day on low activity from Western and domestic investors.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index opened slightly up at 555.66 after closing on Thursday at 555.23.

"The market is overall fairly nervous -- it is moving on broker speculation," said Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkikvadze. "I think it is unlikely it will rise significantly by the end of the day."
Traders saw trade in LUKoil LKOH.RTS as slightly more active, and the share price rose to $28.05 from $27.50 on Thursday.
National power company UES EESR.RTS firmed to $0.4505 at 0950 GMT from $0.4425 previously and regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS ticked up to $1.724 from $.710.
Mosenergo announced on Friday pretax profits to Russian cash standards rose in the first half of the year to 2.44 trillion roubles from 2.01 trillion roubles.

Regional telecom Uralsvyazinform URSI.RTS, which rose to $0.091 after $0.086, said net profits to Russian accruals standards for the first six months of the year rose to 126.6 billion roubles from 82.7 billion roubles.
ICFI-Moscow senior equity trader Dmitry Konov said market players were taking their lead from movements on Wall Street in the absence of a strong trend.

"There is no active interest either from Western or Russian operators and so the market is weakly following the Dow Jones," Konov said. The Dow Jones index rose 13.71 points on Thursday to close at 7942.03.
He added the market could rise next week on investor confidence that a forthcoming U.S. Federal Reserve meeting would not lead to a rise in interest rates.
"The latest U.S. PPI and CPI figures announced on Wednesday and Thursday reinforced confidence that they will not raise interest rates on August 19," he said.
"I think the market will be a little higher by the end of the day and next week it could start to grow."
